name: OPA210 / OPA2210 / OPA4210 (TI 36 V super-beta precision bipolar, 2.2 nV/rtHz)
tagline: TI's 2018 super-beta bipolar successor to the OPAx209: 2.2 nV/rtHz, low 1/f noise and uV-level offset on 36 V. Sold as an upgrade for the Hagerman Bugle MC phono stage.
technology: Super-beta complementary-bipolar precision op-amp on TI's precision process. It runs from up to 36 V (+/-18 V) and has 2.2 nV/rtHz noise, 18 MHz GBW, 6.4 V/us slew, 5 uV typ / 35 uV max offset, 300 pA input bias and 2.2 mA typ supply current per amplifier. The draft's rail-to-rail output claim is not confirmed by web search.

part_numbers.notes: First member of the family, in datasheet rev * (Sep 2018). Packages: SOIC-8 (D; orderable OPA2210ID/IDR), VSSOP-8 (DGK; OPA2210IDGKR) and SON (DRG, moved from preview to production in rev E, Nov 2020). TI makes no DIP-8 version, so DIP8 'rolling' units are SOIC-on-adapter builds.
Added to the datasheet as advanced information (preview) in D and DGK packages in a revision before E. Rev H (Aug 2021) moved the DBV (SOT-23-5) and DGK (VSSOP-8) packages to production.
Unconfirmed. Web search found no TI product page or datasheet mention. The current OPAx210 datasheet abstract names only the OPA210 and OPA2210.

lineage.notes: TI's datasheet calls the OPA210 and OPA2210 'the next generation of OPAx209'.
OPA2210 released with datasheet rev * (Sep 2018). The OPA210 single was added later, and its production packages were complete by rev H (Aug 2021).

key_specs.condition: headline figure (typ vs max not established)

reputation.summary: Praise comes mainly from the phono and DIY scene. Jim Hagerman (Hagerman Audio Labs) sells an OPA2210 upgrade for his Bugle MC phono preamp, which promises about 6 dB less noise. A TNT-Audio reviewer who tested the upgraded Bugle MC wrote that he was surprised how different it sounded. Audiophonics sells the OPA2210 as a DIP8 rolling unit, and its user reviews report more clarity and better bass, with some caveats. The part also comes up in diyAudio's I/V op-amp discussions. Head-Fi reports are mixed: one user got hum after a swap, and another heard no difference from the LM833 or OPA2107.
sonic_descriptors: lower noise in MC phono use (Hagerman/TNT-Audio)
typical_uses: MC phono preamp gain stage (Hagerman Bugle MC upgrade)
I/V stage after a current-output DAC (diyAudio discussion)
op-amp rolling via DIP8 adapter units
caveats: The DIP8 versions are SOIC-on-adapter builds; TI makes no DIP package.
Head-Fi: one user reported hum after a swap, and another heard no difference from the LM833 or OPA2107.
The praise rests on a small number of sources.
